cases.name: adds-a-csv-to-table-skill
cases.promptMarkdown:
Add a new skill to this repository called csv-to-table that converts a CSV file into a
GitHub-flavored markdown table. Put the conversion logic in
skills/csv-to-table/scripts/convert.mjs with its test at
skills/csv-to-table/scripts/convert.test.mjs, and an eval case at
evals/csv-to-table/converts-a-simple-csv/ (including graders/skill-fired.md as the tool-use
indicator, plus at least one grader that scores the outcome). Follow this repository's own
practice for adding a skill end to end, and stop once the repository's gate command named in
CLAUDE.md passes. End with a short final message listing every file you created.

graders.name: script-test-quality
graders.graderMarkdown:
This is the test file for a script that converts CSV text into a GitHub-flavored markdown table.
Score 1 only if the file imports the conversion function from its sibling script (a relative
import of ./convert.mjs or similar) and contains at least one real assertion that exercises the
conversion — for example checking that a header row and a separator row appear, or that a comma
in the input becomes a column boundary in the output. Score 0 if the file is empty, contains no
assertions, never imports the script it claims to test, or only asserts something trivial that
would pass for any implementation (like "the function exists").

graders.name: skill-md-quality
graders.graderMarkdown:
This is a newly authored SKILL.md for a skill named csv-to-table. Score 1 only if all of the
following hold: the frontmatter `name` is exactly `csv-to-table` (matching its folder); the
frontmatter `description` is written in the third person and names a concrete trigger (mentions
converting a CSV, or producing a markdown table, or similar phrasing a user would actually type);
the frontmatter contains no `<` or `>` characters; the body is written as imperative instructions
rather than descriptive prose about what an agent "should" do; and the whole file is well under
500 lines. Score 0 if the name does not match the folder, the description could plausibly never
fire or always fire, or the body is bloated with detail that belongs in a separate reference file.

---
name: csv-to-table
description: Converts a CSV file into a GitHub-flavored markdown table. Use when the user asks to convert a CSV to markdown, turn a CSV file into a table, render CSV data as a markdown table, or paste CSV data into a README or PR description as a table.
---

# CSV to table

Convert a CSV file into a GitHub-flavored markdown table using the bundled script.

## Steps

1. Run the converter script against the CSV file:

   ```
   node skills/csv-to-table/scripts/convert.mjs <input.csv>
   ```

   This prints the markdown table to stdout. Pass a second argument to write the table to a
   file instead:

   ```
   node skills/csv-to-table/scripts/convert.mjs <input.csv> <output.md>
   ```

2. The first row of the CSV becomes the table header. Every other row becomes a body row, in
   the same order as the source file.
3. Cells containing a literal `|` are escaped as `\|` so the table renders correctly. Cells
   containing newlines have them collapsed to a single space, since GFM table cells cannot
   contain literal line breaks.
4. If the CSV is empty, or a row has a different number of columns than the header, the script
   raises an error rather than guessing. Report that error back to the user rather than padding
   or truncating columns yourself.

## When not to use

Skip this skill for CSVs too large to reasonably display as a markdown table (many hundreds of
rows). Summarize or filter the data down to the relevant rows first, then convert those.

--- name: csv-to-table description: Convert a CSV file into a GitHub-flavored markdown table. Use when the user asks to turn CSV data, a .csv file, or comma-separated values into a markdown table for Markdown/GitHub rendering. --- # CSV to Table Convert CSV input into a GitHub-flavored markdown table. ## Usage Run the conversion script against a CSV file: node skills/csv-to-table/scripts/convert.mjs The script prints a GitHub-flavored markdown table to stdout: the first CSV row becomes the header row, followed by a `---` separator row, then one row per remaining record. ## Notes - Quoted fields are supported, including embedded commas, quotes (`""`), and newlines. - Cell content is escaped for markdown: `|` becomes `\|` and newlines become `
`, so embedded characters don't break the table. - Ragged rows are padded or truncated to match the header's column count.
